description: Closed regression lock for every adjudicated deletion of a derived wire field: a member that a ruling removed from a schema object because it is a pure function of members that stay on the wire (or of the enclosing carrier), and whose transcript or verifier role, if any, is now filled by recomputation. Each row pins one exact (schema, path, removed) triple: the removed member MUST NOT return to that object's properties or required (directly or through an allOf/oneOf/anyOf/if-then-else overlay of the same object) and the declared source member MUST remain declared. The lock never infers semantics from field names; a row exists only because a ruling named the exact path.

registry_rules.path_rule: path is the JSON Pointer (without the leading #) of the schema object that owned the removed member: empty string for the file root, otherwise /$defs/<name>[/properties/<member>|/items|/oneOf/<index>...]. It MUST resolve to a schema object.
registry_rules.removed_rule: removed names one member. The member MUST be absent from the resolved object's properties and required, and from the properties and required of every allOf, oneOf, anyOf, if, then and else branch that overlays the same object; nested property subschemas are not searched.
registry_rules.source_rule: source names the member whose bytes the deleted value is recomputed from. source.field is required; source.schema and source.path default to the row's own schema and path and MAY point at another object (for example the Event envelope root when a payload member was a projection of envelope.actor_id). The source member MUST remain declared in that object's explicit property set. When the ruling replaced the deleted member with a new one (E5 winner_index), the replacement is the source and the lock is red until the replacement lands.
registry_rules.derivation_rule: derivation states the pure function or the transcript injection that replaces the wire member, in the words of the ruling; it is documentation for implementers and is not machine-evaluated.
registry_rules.spec_anchor_rule: spec_anchor MUST be a spec/v1/zh prose path, optionally with #<heading-slug>; the file MUST exist and the heading, when given, MUST exist. ruling is a short label of the adjudication (review report date-time id plus item) and is never a repository path.
registry_rules.division_of_labor: Sibling digests deleted under zh/conformance/encoding.md 4.0.1 (a bare digest next to a complete content-addressed typed ref) are locked exclusively by tools/artifact_lint/schemas.py CONTENT_ADDRESSED_REF_MIRROR_REMOVALS, owned by the 2026-09-02-1948 ruling, and MUST NOT be duplicated here; the lint fails a row that repeats one of those triples. This lock carries every other adjudicated derived-field deletion: same-carrier projections, constant families, proof-envelope metadata mirrors, AEAD header digests and cross-carrier projections of envelope members.

No hidden alternate digest is added to the closed account-registration or identity-creation proof transcript. When another contract requires the full method_history_head, compute it from the exact verified method entry/document. WebVH versionId entryHash excludes proof and substitutes the predecessor versionId, so decoding it cannot produce the complete signed-entry JCS digest. Synthetic did:web/did:key commitments retain their registered adapter rules.
